title: Airlines Cut Diwali Flights For First Time Since Covid As Fares Surge
excerpt: Cirium data reported by Bloomberg put October–November scheduled flights about 6% below a year earlier, while a separate weekly domestic count also fell — with fares on some routes doubling in effect.
body:
• Airlines scheduled about 6% fewer flights across October and November than a year earlier, according to Cirium data reported by Bloomberg via The Hindu BusinessLine — the first capacity decline since 2020, when capacity fell by nearly 45% in the pandemic.
  • A separate Business Standard count of weekly domestic flights for November put the total at 22,306, down 606 or 2.6% — a different measure from the Cirium October–November figure, with Air India cutting the most weekly flights.
  • Domestic passenger traffic had already declined 6.5% in September, and festive fares on some routes surged to levels where a one-way ticket cost as much as a round trip a year ago, BusinessLine reported.
  • For travellers with India trips booked: recheck your flight times before travelling, as schedules can still change — and expect fewer choices and higher fares on thinner routes.

India's airlines operated fewer routes during the peak Diwali travel season, signalling that rising costs and operational disruptions are beginning to cool momentum in one of the world's fastest growing aviation markets, Bloomberg reported via The Hindu BusinessLine.

Airlines scheduled about 6% fewer flights across October and November than a year earlier, according to data from aviation analytics firm Cirium cited in that report. That marks the first capacity decline since 2020, when carriers slashed service capacity by nearly 45% amid the pandemic-induced collapse in travel demand.

Two counts, two different measures

A separate, earlier count helps explain the domestic picture, but it is not the same number. I-Journey, citing a Business Standard analysis published November 1, reported 22,306 weekly domestic flights scheduled for November 2026, down 606 from 22,912, a 2.6% drop. In that weekly domestic count, Air India trimmed 543 weekly flights, or 14.9%, from 3,644 to 3,101; IndiGo cut 375 flights, or 2.7%, to 13,697; Air India Express dropped 78 to 2,420; and SpiceJet cut 37 to 679. The Cirium figure covers October and November overall, while the Business Standard figure counts weekly domestic flights in November — readers should not treat them as conflicting or interchangeable.

Why fares rose as flights fell

While domestic passenger traffic had already declined 6.5% in September, festive-season fares on some routes surged to levels where one-way tickets cost as much as round-trip journeys did a year ago, BusinessLine reported.

"One-way fares had crossed Rs 20,000 ($213), roughly what I would normally pay for a round trip."

— Dinesh Sharma, traveller quoted by Bloomberg via BusinessLine

Sharma, a 28-year-old marketing professional in Hyderabad travelling home to Siliguri in West Bengal, told Bloomberg he could not find an affordable ticket despite booking months in advance. Airlines say demand remains resilient but acknowledged passengers are bearing higher costs. IndiGo chief executive Willie Walsh said on an earnings call last month that demand had held up "reasonably well," while noting airlines had to balance affordability with financial stability, BusinessLine reported.

IndiGo, India's largest carrier, reduced capacity by 1% and carried 4.5% fewer passengers during the quarter ended September, according to the same report. Despite a more than 34% increase in passenger yields, it reported a loss of Rs 1,880 crore as its fuel bill jumped 67%. The report attributed the cost squeeze to higher fuel prices, a weaker rupee and longer international flight paths caused by airspace restrictions, citing Mumbai travel agency chief Ajay Prakash of Nomad Travels.

What this means for your trip

On thinner routes the weekly domestic count showed sharper drops — Delhi to Hyderabad fell from 408 to 322 weekly flights and Hyderabad to Tirupati lost 86 weekly flights in the Business Standard analysis reported by I-Journey, while Patna was scheduled for 302 weekly departures against 377 a year earlier. Travellers on secondary routes may find fewer options and less fare competition.

The practical step is narrow and sourced: schedules can still change, so recheck flight times with your airline before heading to the airport, as I-Journey's report advised. No booking link is offered here beyond the reporting linked above, because no airline schedule page was part of the sources for this story.
